title: I made a steampunk survivors-like game, looking for feedback
author: PositiveCouple1814
selftext:
I used AI but by no means the game was made by it, I touched every graphic asset, I worked all sounds, made my own sprite sheets, made the lore, optimized code, etc, etc, etc. 

* **Game Title:** Punk, bullets and Junk (PB&J)
* **Playable Link:** [https://pewpew4u.itch.io/punk-bullets-and-junk](https://pewpew4u.itch.io/punk-bullets-and-junk)
* **Platform:** Windows PC
* **Description:** (Provide a detailed description of your game. Minimum 100 words) **Free Demo available and Full game released at 81% discount**
* **Status:** Released full game and demo
* **Involvement:** Solo developer

There is a full blog post about the game you can find here:  
[https://pewpew4u.itch.io/punk-bullets-and-junk/devlog/1570892/finally-got-to-release-pbj](https://pewpew4u.itch.io/punk-bullets-and-junk/devlog/1570892/finally-got-to-release-pbj)

Side note... what's up with all those people spreading hate just because you used a tool? I spent a lot of months, long nights, weekends and every minute of my free time, but instead of providing feedback, I get people calling all this effort "soulless ai slop" without even trying the demo, like if I woke up and single prompt made the game (WTF?!!).

comments.author: kernet
comments.body: What is the tech stack and workflow?

replies.author: PositiveCouple1814
replies.body:
Well... the actual things I'm going to replicate that gave me the best results is to first create the lore in NotebookLM so you can have a nice and tight structure, at least for me this part was fundamental, because I like to know what I'm going to do and I like to have coherent stories, this also make things easier as you don't have to bang your head in the wall creating new stuff because the story guides you.

Then, unfortunately image generation wasn't great for me, I ended up using gimp heavily, I even used batch processing (which is a bit different in the newest version but totally worth learning) and gave me great results, AI does give you a good base but for every asset that ended up in the game I went through a lot of ideas and experiments and changes, but yeah, using gimp is an absolute must, even for cleaning pictures, I found AI is a disaster to say the least, I touched every asset.

For music I have a collection of assets and there are a lot of creative commons free for commercial use, but for me audacity is an absolute must, many times you can create multiple sound effects from a simple sound, I really didn't bother making SFX with AI, I don't need it for sound, if any, I think I'll go back to my FLStudio+Audacity combo.

Then you go through the game itself with the engine of your preference and from here it depends on your style, but if your game is very performance dependent as mine, then yes or yes you have to verify the code, specially the way on how memory is used, AI can do code, but is not great at architecture, so, your primary asset is to research on the weaknesses of your engine and how to optimize memory usage, optimize collisions, experiment with whiskers and other methods to let your mobs move around and by far with AI you have to test, test, test, test, test, test, test and some more testing at the end to make sure things look and feel good.
